class: A user-facing statement of WHERE a strategy loses money that is chosen from the breakevens (their count, and the sign of the P&L at one or a few sample points) instead of from the regions where the expiry P&L is actually negative is wrong whenever the P&L touches or sits at zero (a zero-premium spread, a ratio, a debit equal to the width, a plateau) or loses in more regions than the breakeven count implies; breakevens are where P&L crosses zero, loss regions are where P&L < 0, and the two stop matching exactly in those shapes.
mechanism: W-063 chose 'outside'/'between' by expiry_pnl_at((lo+up)/2) > 0 (one sample); W-066 round 4 compared the lowest P&L 0.01 outside each breakeven with the lowest just inside; the one-breakeven path (_lower_upper, scenario/levels.py) picks 'above'/'below' from the breakeven alone. Each rule is a heuristic over breakevens, so each new shape breaks it.

Tier A verifier (route POST 200 for 3): 1x2 put ratio -> 'below 22,000 or above 22,400' (P&L exactly 0 above 22,400); two call butterflies -> 'between 22,300 and 22,900' (also loses outside); zero-cost bull call spread (max loss 0.00) -> 'below 22,800'; butterfly costing its width -> 'above 22,300' (loses both sides). Round-1 (midpoint) and round-2 (_loses_outside) both red: second occurrence of the class within W-066.
